I've been farming these 5 mu in Quzhou for 35 years, and it's all cotton. Last year I planted the improved Bt cotton seeds that the input dealer in town sells — the kind my neighbor Lao Wang also uses. They resist bollworm pretty well. I put down 3 jin of seed per mu. I harvested about 550 jin of seed cotton per mu, which was decent. Not my best year, but the price was okay so I didn't lose money.

This year I'm sticking with the same improved variety. I learned a long time ago not to change what works. For fertilizer, I spread one full bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's 50 kg per mu. It gives me nitrogen, phosphate, and potassium all together. When the cotton starts flowering in July, I top-dress with urea, about 20 jin per mu. The dealer told me years ago that flowering cotton needs extra nitrogen, and I've done it ever since. I don't buy separate phosphate or potash fertilizer — the compound fertilizer has enough, and every extra bag is money I can't spend on pesticide or hired labor. With only two people in my house, I have to pay help to pick in autumn, and that's 150 yuan per mu or more.

Irrigation: I have a well, but pumping costs electricity. I irrigate twice — once right after planting in late April to get the seeds up, and once in mid-July when the bolls are setting. If the summer rains are good, I might get by without the second one, but cotton is thirsty when it's flowering, and I'd rather waste some water than lose yield.

Pesticide: I spray 12 times. Cotton draws every bug in the county. Even with the Bt seeds, I still get aphids early, then spider mites, and some bollworms later when the resistance wears off. I start in early June and spray every 10 days until late August. Each spray costs about 35 yuan for the chemical, so that's over 400 yuan per mu. I also need plastic mulch — I always lay the thin film because it warms the soil and keeps weeds down. That's another cost I factor into my budget.

Tillage: I rotary till in mid-April before planting. Deep plowing is too slow, and my cousin tried no-tillage once — the weeds were a disaster.

I expect to get about 275 kg per mu this year. Last year I got about the same, 550 jin. I always plan for what I know I can get. I never cut back on fertilizer to save money. A bad harvest means I can't pay my bills. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost.
